messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Algorithm
parts:
Hi all,

In BUGS and JAGS, for a simple models such as linear regression, we know that the algorithm using Gibbs or MH samplers to sample the posterior. In standard book, we can see how BUGS or JAGS work in such simple example. I would like to find books or articles which give clear explanation (step by step) how stan work in a particular (and simple) example.

Could you suggest some of them?

Thank you so much!

Tran.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Algorithm
parts:
There's a brief intro in the manual.

Radford Neal's paper in the MCMC handbook or McKay's
chapters in his Information Theory book are good intros
to HMC. Then you need to read the NUTS paper of Hoffman
and Gelman, then Michael Betancourt's papers on arXiv.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Algorithm
parts:
Note that the vanilla HMC algorithm is straightforward to write down
in a few lines of pseudo code, but it is not particularly effective.  What
makes Stan perform so well are more sophisticated implementations 
of the HMC method which quickly become more complex.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Algorithm
parts:
There is an example of HMC programmed from scratch in appendix C of BDA3.  Section C.4.  This example is not identical to Stan, as Stan uses the no-U-turn sampler and our example uses HMC with fixed step size and number of steps, but it will at least give a sense of how HMC works.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Algorithm
parts:
I've never coded MATLAB in my life, but I find MacKay's MATLAB
code easier to read than R because it uses native vector
notation like Stan (along with the kind of unconventional
spacing R programmers seem to favor):

http://www.inference.phy.cam.ac.uk/mackay/itprnn/ps/492.503.pdf

Here's the chapter from Andrew's book:

http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/book/software.pdf

Read both! It's always helpful to see the same algorithm in
several different notations.

- Bob
